<!-- question-type: inclass -->
### Exercise 5: Requesting data for many years

We now have a function that can request one indicator for one year. Suppose we want life expectancy for Australia every five years from 1960 to 2020.

**(a)** Create a vector called `years` containing the years from 1960 to 2020 in steps of five.

```{r}
#| eval: false

years <-
  seq(
    from = YOUR_CODE,
    to = YOUR_CODE,
    by = 5
  )
```

**(b)** Without using `map()`, use `get_indicator()` to request life expectancy for the first three years in `years`. What is changing across these three calls of the function? What is staying the same?


```{r}
#| eval: false

YOUR_CODE_HERE
```


**(c)** Use `map()` to repeat the request for every value in `years`.

```{r}
#| eval: false

life_expectancy <-
  map(
    YOUR_CODE,
    YOUR_CODE,
    indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
  )
```

**(d)** Inspect `life_expectancy`.

What type of object has `map()` returned?

**(e)** Use `list_rbind()` to combine the results into one dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false

life_expectancy <-
  life_expectancy |>
  YOUR_CODE
```

<!-- BEGIN PROFILE:r-teaching-guide -->
::: {.content-visible when-profile="r-teaching-guide"}

::: {.teaching-block}

::: {.teaching-block-header}
Teaching Note
:::

::: {.teaching-block-body}

🎯 **Learning Objective**

Students should:

- create a sequence of years using `seq()`;
- use `map()` to repeat the same function over multiple years;
- recognise which part of the function call changes across iterations and which part stays fixed;
- recognise that `map()` returns a list;
- combine the returned datasets using `list_rbind()`.

✅ **Core Concepts to Highlight**

- The three manual calls in part (b) all use the same function and indicator.
- Only the value of `year` changes across those calls.
- `map()` automates this repeated pattern.
- Here, `map()` works through each value in `years` and calls `get_indicator()` once for each value.
- The indicator stays fixed at `"SP.DYN.LE00.IN"` across all calls.
- `map()` returns one result for each year, stored in a list.
- `list_rbind()` combines those results into one dataset.

💬 **Suggested In-Class Prompts**

- How many times will `get_indicator()` be called?
- What will the first call made by `map()` look like?
- What will the second call look like?
- Which part of the function call changes from one request to the next?
- Why does `map()` return more than one object?

📌 **Common Misunderstandings**

- Thinking that the full `years` vector is passed to `get_indicator()` in a single call.
- Thinking that the indicator changes across calls.
- Expecting `map()` to return one data frame directly.
- Forgetting that each call to `get_indicator()` returns its own dataset.

:::

:::

:::
<!-- END PROFILE:r-teaching-guide -->

<!-- BEGIN PROFILE:r-solutions -->
::: {.content-visible when-profile="r-solutions" when-profile="r-teaching-guide"}

::: {.solution-block}

::: {.solution-block-header}
Solution
:::

::: {.solution-block-body}

(a)

```{r}
years <-
  seq(
    from = 1960,
    to = 2020,
    by = 5
  )
```

(b)

```{r}
get_indicator(
  year = 1960,
  indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
)

get_indicator(
  year = 1965,
  indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
)

get_indicator(
  year = 1970,
  indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
)
```

The year changes across the three calls. The indicator stays the same.

(c)

```{r}
life_expectancy <-
  map(
    years,
    get_indicator,
    indicator = "SP.DYN.LE00.IN"
  )
```

(d)

`map()` returns a list. Each element contains the result of one call to `get_indicator()`.

(e)

```{r}
life_expectancy <-
  life_expectancy |>
  list_rbind()
```

:::

:::

:::
